text.p: Creditors of Espebepe will meet again on May 16 to decide on a debt write-off for the troubled construction firm after they failed to come to an agreement on Monday for technical reasons, a company source said.
The source, who asked not to be named, said more than half of the creditors were represented at the Monday meeting, but the number fell short of the required 80 percent of capital ownd.

Espebepe wants to write off 95 percent of 75 million zloty debt, saying it is the only way to prevent bankruptcy. It would be the first bankruptcy for a company listed on the Polish bourse since it was restored in 1991.

Espebepe's largest creditor, Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS), on Friday said the debt restructuring proposal was unacceptable. It said the company should consider the bank's earlier suggestion of combining a debt write-off with a debt- for-equity swap through a convertible bond issue -- a plan Espebepe's management rejected as too time consuming.
